features.title: In-place workspaces and a per-project start folder

appProof.steps: Build in e2e mode (VITE_EXPOSE_STORE=true npx electron-vite build --mode e2e) and run an untracked tests/e2e/zz-proof-in-place.spec.ts, copied from .claude/skills/orca-test-and-verify/assets/proof-shots.spec.template.ts, with SKIP_BUILD=1 ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1 pnpm exec playwright test --config tests/playwright.config.ts --project electron-headless so the window stays hidden and screenshots come from page.screenshot over CDP. In the fixture repo create a services/api folder, then call window.__store.getState().updateRepo(repoId, { inPlaceWorkspaces: true, workspaceStartPath: 'services/api' }). Screenshot 1: open Settings with state.openSettingsTarget({ pane: 'repo', repoId }) plus openSettingsPage(); it should show the switch Create workspaces without git worktrees turned on and the Start folder input reading services/api. Screenshot 2: open the sidebar composer (openSidebarWorkspaceComposer helper), type a name and click Create Workspace; the composer should show no branch or base fields, and the sidebar should list the root checkout row plus the new workspace row (data-worktree-id contains ::workspace:), with the header tooltip Create workspace for <project>. Screenshot 3: createTerminalTabFromMenu, execInTerminal 'pwd', and capture output ending in /services/api; record git worktree list --porcelain before and after into JSON to show no new git worktree. Screenshot 4: delete the workspace from the sidebar (dialog copy should say it only forgets the entry), then show the root row still present and services/api still on disk. For the subfolder add, call window.api.repos.add({ path: <repo>/services/api, kind: 'git' }) on a throwaway git repo and record repo.path (the git root), repo.displayName (api) and repo.workspaceStartPath. BEFORE is the same spec against an upstream/main build, where the setting is ignored: the sidebar shows a git worktree and the terminal starts at the checkout root. Use only disposable fixtures; delete the throwaway workspace and repo afterwards.

Use the e2e-mode build and an untracked tests/e2e/zz-proof-vertical-tabs.spec.ts based on proof-shots.spec.template.ts (SKIP_BUILD=1 ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1 playwright --project electron-headless, hidden window, page.screenshot over CDP). Reuse createBrowserSplitWithTabs from tests/e2e/vertical-tab-strip.spec.ts: ensureWorktreeRootGroup, createEmptySplitGroup(..., 'right'), then three createBrowserTab(worktreeId, 'about:blank', { targetGroupId }) calls and focusGroup. Screenshot 1 (horizontal): the right pane shows its three tabs in the normal strip. Click the button named Show tabs on the side inside [data-tab-group-strip-id=<groupId>]. Screenshot 2 should show a 13rem column on the left of that pane with a New tab row at the top, three stacked full-width rows with a 2px active marker on the left edge of the active row, and the browser body starting to the right of the column; record orientation and rect boxes to JSON. Drag the last row onto the top half of the first (mouse.down/move/up with steps) and screenshot 3 with the new order while group count stays 2. Finally click Show tabs on top and screenshot 4 showing the horizontal strip back. BEFORE (upstream/main) has no toggle button, so the same spec records only the horizontal strip.

features.title: Local builds skip background update checks

appProof.steps: This is packaged-only behaviour (it depends on app.getVersion() carrying -local.<timestamp>.<commit>), so use .claude/skills/orca-test-and-verify/scripts/packaged-proof.sh against the installed local build (/Applications/Orca.app or dist/mac-*/Orca.app built by package-and-install.sh) launched hidden with ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1, a throwaway profile and --use-mock-keychain: packaged-proof.sh <Orca.app> <out.png> --wait-for '[aria-label="Update available"]' --timeout 60000 --report-js 'Promise.all([window.api.updater.getVersion(), window.api.updater.getStatus()])'. The report should show a version containing -local. and a status that never becomes available/downloading, with found=false and a screenshot of the idle app with no Update available affordance. Then run --report-js 'window.api.updater.check().then(() => window.api.updater.getStatus())' to show an explicit check still goes to checking/idle or error rather than being blocked. BEFORE is the same script against an upstream/main packaged build (or the same app with a version stripped of the local suffix), which shows the Update available affordance after the startup check. Do not click any install button.

features.title: Okta FastPass in the built-in browser

appProof.steps: A real Okta sign-in cannot be driven in CI or hidden screenshots, so say so in the report and prove the permission surface instead. Launch the e2e build hidden (SKIP_BUILD=1 ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1 playwright --project electron-headless) with an untracked zz-proof-okta.spec.ts that, like tests/e2e/browser-site-notification-mute.spec.ts, uses electronApp.evaluate to session.fromPartition('persist:orca-browser').protocol.handle('https', ...) to serve a probe page, opens it with window.__store.getState().createBrowserTab(worktreeId, 'https://okta-probe.example.test/', { activate: true }), and from the webview runs navigator.permissions.query for local-network-access and loopback-network (record state or the TypeError) and fetch('http://127.0.0.1:<port>/') against a tiny Node server started by the spec, with a screenshot of the tab. Also show the main-process side by running the focused unit tests (vitest on browser-session-registry.persistence.test.ts and the new policy tests) and quote the green output in the report. BEFORE (upstream/main) records denied/blocked for the loopback fetch and permission, AFTER records granted/success. Ask the owner to confirm the real Okta FastPass sign-in by hand.

Mirror tests/e2e/browser-side-pane.spec.ts: ensureTerminalVisible, terminalGroupId = ensureWorktreeRootGroup(worktreeId), then window.__store.getState().openNewBrowserTabInActiveWorkspace(terminalGroupId). Screenshot 1 after the first call: the terminal keeps the left half and a new right pane shows a vertical tab list with one New Browser Tab row. Record layoutByWorktree, browserGroupIds and orientationByGroup (terminal pane null, side pane 'vertical') to JSON. Call it again from the terminal group (second row appears in the same pane, still two groups) and once from the side pane group (third row) and screenshot 2. Also trigger a link route by evaluating openHttpLink-equivalent state (window.__store createBrowserTab(worktreeId, 'https://example.com/', { activate: true, placement: 'side-pane' })) and, if a local dev port is listening, openWorkspacePortInBrowser from the Ports panel, to show those land in the same pane. BEFORE (upstream/main) opens the browser as a tab beside the terminal tabs in the single pane, so the same spec records one group.

features.title: Slack page notifications muted in the browser

appProof.steps: The committed e2e spec is the proof template: run it as an untracked copy (tests/e2e/zz-proof-slack-mute.spec.ts) with SKIP_BUILD=1 ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1 playwright --project electron-headless so everything stays hidden. It registers session.fromPartition('persist:orca-browser').protocol.handle('https', ...) through electronApp.evaluate to serve a probe page, opens https://app.slack.com/client and a control https://notify.example.test/ with window.__store.getState().createBrowserTab(worktreeId, url, { activate: true }), and reads Notification.permission and await Notification.requestPermission() inside each webview. Record both pairs to JSON (Slack: denied/denied, control: granted/granted) and screenshot each tab (page.screenshot over CDP) so the page title Notify probe is visible. Also screenshot the app after the Slack request to show no permission-denied notice or banner appeared. BEFORE (upstream/main) records granted/granted for the Slack origin. Never open the real Slack web app in the proof; use the served probe page.

features.title: Nest one project's workspaces across hosts

appProof.steps: Needs one project registered on two hosts: a local checkout and an SSH checkout with the same git origin (Docker sshd relay target via tests/e2e/helpers/docker-ssh-relay-target.ts, or a real devbox). Launch the app hidden with ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1 in e2e mode (window.__store exposed), attach Playwright over CDP, wait until both main worktrees report the same projectId, call window.__store.getState().setGroupBy("repo"), then drag the card [data-worktree-drag-id=<ssh id>] onto [data-worktree-card-parent-content] of the local card with CDP mouse events. The AFTER screenshot should show the local card with a "Hide 1 child workspace" chip and the SSH workspace indented one level beneath it; check worktreeLineageById[sshId].parentWorktreeId equals the local id. BEFORE screenshot is the same view with both cards at depth 0. Then open the delete dialog on the local parent: the "delete with children" list must not include the SSH child. Restart the app and confirm the nesting survives (hydration lists the edge under the SSH host snapshot).

features.title: Okta Verify ports forwarded to the desktop from SSH tabs

appProof.steps: Needs an SSH host (Docker sshd relay target or real devbox) connected in Orca with a workspace on it, and the setting that routes SSH-workspace browser tabs through the SSH host (Settings, Browser, SSH workspace routing) left on. Launch hidden with ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1 and e2e mode, attach over CDP. On the desktop start a small http stub on 127.0.0.1:65123 (or the first free Okta port from the end of the list) answering "desktop-authenticator" with access-control-allow-origin: *. In the SSH workspace create a browser tab with window.__store.getState().createBrowserTab(worktreeId, url, {activate: true}), then run fetch("http://127.0.0.1:65123/probe") inside the guest via the webview executeJavaScript and fetch("http://127.0.0.1:18080/...") against a port that only the SSH host serves. Expected: the first returns desktop-authenticator, the second lands in the SSH host fixture log. Capture the evaluated values plus a CDP screenshot of the browser tab as proof. A real Okta FastPass sign-in cannot be proven without Okta Verify installed, so say so in the report.

features.title: iOS build reports its entitled APNs environment

appProof.steps: iOS Simulator against an isolated headless host (AGENTS.md recipe: build the desktop with package-and-install.sh without --install, run dist/mac-arm64/Orca.app --serve --mobile-pairing with a SHORT profile dir, --use-mock-keychain, ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1). Make the host's push gateway observable: set ORCA_PUSH_GATEWAY_URL to a local node stub that logs POST bodies (plain http is accepted only for an unpackaged host; a packaged dist app needs an https origin, so use the self-hosted gateway orca-push.bell.drakestears.com and read `docker logs orca-push` instead). Build the phone app as a Release (non-__DEV__) simulator build twice, BEFORE at 6ab006ddd8^ and AFTER at HEAD, without ORCA_IOS_APS_ENVIRONMENT (development entitlement), pair via `xcrun simctl openurl`, then turn push on in the phone's notification settings. Capture the notifications.registerPush body: BEFORE shows apnsEnvironment 'production', AFTER shows 'sandbox'; rebuilding AFTER with ORCA_IOS_APS_ENVIRONMENT=production shows 'production'. Screenshot the settings toggle plus a terminal/log capture of the request body as the proof. Cheap corroboration without a device: `ORCA_IOS_APS_ENVIRONMENT=production npx expo config --type introspect` (prints extra.apsEnvironment next to the entitlement). If the simulator cannot mint an APNs token (getDevicePushTokenAsync rejects, so registration is skipped), state that plainly and fall back to a physical device build.

features.title: Claude usage credits in the status bar without windows

appProof.steps: Desktop launched hidden from an e2e-mode build (VITE_EXPOSE_STORE=true electron-vite build --mode e2e; ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1; Playwright electron-headless over CDP; screenshots with page.screenshot, never computer-use). Seed disposable state only: through window.__store.getState().setRateLimitsFromPush({ ...state.rateLimits, claude: { provider: 'claude', session: null, weekly: null, extraUsage: { unit: 'currency', balance: 980.4, currencyCode: 'USD', spent: 19.6, spendLimit: 1000, spentPercent: 1.96, enabled: true, disabledReason: null, resetsAt: null }, status: 'ok', ... } }) exactly as tests/e2e/status-bar-credit-usage.spec.ts does. BEFORE (588b9ea756^): the footer .status-bar-usage-cluster [data-usage-chip="claude"] is a bare icon and the 'Usage' popover row says 'No usage data'. AFTER: the chip reads '$19.60 / $1,000' with a spend bar and the popover row shows the same text plus a 'credits' bar at 2%. Then check the edge states by pushing variants: balance only (no spend limit) -> '$980.40 bal' without a bar; status 'error' on the same snapshot -> text stays with a warning triangle; shrink the window (Playwright setViewportSize or CDP Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride) to see the letter-badge dot and the +N overflow chip title ('Also: Claude $19.60 / $1,000'); and toggle the usage display mode (compact vs verbose) to confirm the bar disappears in compact. The main-process half (credit-only snapshot kept through a failed refresh) has no UI to drive hidden; it is proven by the service unit test.

Exercise the workflow end to end on a disposable trivial renderer change, hidden and background only (ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1, never computer-use): `source .claude/skills/orca-test-and-verify/scripts/env.sh` (confirm Node 24 and ORCA_REPO), copy assets/proof-shots.spec.template.ts to tests/e2e/zz-proof-skill-check.spec.ts, run capture-before-after.sh before then after into a scratch dir (check `git stash list` is empty and the working-tree edit survived), write a manifest.json referencing the before/after PNGs, and build the page twice: `build-report.py manifest.json out-fragment.html --fragment` and without the flag; open out.html through CDP/Playwright (file:// URL) and screenshot to confirm images render, the lightbox opens and the full page has the wrapper while the fragment does not, then publish the fragment through the Artifact tool. Run package-and-install.sh WITHOUT --install and packaged-proof.sh against dist/mac-arm64/Orca.app (hidden, mock keychain, throwaway profile) for a CDP screenshot. To prove the bbf2c429f2 warning, run package-and-install.sh --install on a spare machine/profile with Orca's quit confirmation left open and read the '[install] WARNING' lines; if that cannot be done safely say so. Before trusting the report builder, also run it with /usr/bin/python3 (3.9) to see the str | None TypeError.
